summary: Configured node1 to log all sudo commands with timestamp and user to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, excluded them from general system logs, and verified persistence after reboot.
actions_performed: Added /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-command-logging with a dedicated logfile and sudo syslog disabled.
Set the log to root:adm ownership and mode 0640; validated sudoers with visudo.
Verified live sudo commands include timestamp, invoking user, target user, and command.
Confirmed test entries were absent from /var/log/syslog and /var/log/auth.log.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified configuration and logging recovery.

evidence.requirement: Record sudo commands with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Valid global sudo policy directs logging to the protected file; captured entries show timestamp, invoker antrieb, target USER=root, and full command.

evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of general system logs
evidence.summary: Unique pre- and post-reboot command markers were absent from both /var/log/syslog and /var/log/auth.log.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 8336c3a1-91fc-4135-b26a-5d2863cb2594; reboot was acknowledged; node returned with changed boot ID 8d09cbbb-ee0a-4e05-a31b-0cc05d61303c; sudoers validation, retained data, rsyslog health, new command logging, and log isolation all passed.
